stem: A client has a positive pregnancy test, unilateral lower-abdominal pain, and vaginal bleeding. Which condition must be ruled out promptly?
rationale: ACOG identifies abnormal vaginal bleeding and pelvic or abdominal pain as warning symptoms of ectopic pregnancy in a pregnant patient. Ectopic pregnancy can become life-threatening if it ruptures and therefore requires prompt evaluation.
educational_objective: Recognize symptoms that require prompt evaluation for ectopic pregnancy.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
source_locator: Symptoms / emergency warning signs: abnormal vaginal bleeding and pelvic or abdominal pain in ectopic pregnancy
source_claim_supported: Positive pregnancy with unilateral abdominal/pelvic pain and vaginal bleeding is concerning for ectopic pregnancy and requires evaluation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
correction_summary: Retained the ACOG-supported symptom cluster but removed unnecessarily verbose alternatives and avoided claiming symptoms alone prove the diagnosis.
